extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants and their advisors (legal, accounting, sustainability/compliance teams), investors, and assurance providers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory disclosure criteria for U.S. public company registrants under the SEC's final climate-related disclosure rules, covering risks, governance, targets, metrics (GHG), assurance, scenario analysis, transition plans, and related procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science-based GHG emissions reduction targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the registrant has disclosed its ambition and engagement related to setting science-based GHG emissions reduction targets. Emissions targets are considered science-based if they align with the goals of the Paris Climate Agreement to limit warming to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. That is, whether the company has explicitly disclosed that they have either committed to setting or have set science-based targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information is typically sourced from a company's CSR report. The rule treats explicit commitments or set targets that align with Paris goals as 'science-based'. Registrants should clearly state if they have committed to or set such targets to enable investor comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net Zero ambition and engagement disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the registrant has disclosed its ambition and engagement related to achieving Net Zero GHG emissions. Net Zero refers to a state in which GHG emissions released into the atmosphere are balanced by removal of emissions from the atmosphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bloomberg and other data providers source this from CSR reports. Registrants should disclose whether they have Net Zero plans or ambitions; data show adoption varies by company size (e.g., lower incidence among smaller registrants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party assurance of climate-related disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and to what extent registrants have obtained third-party assurance or verification of their climate-related disclosures (including the scope of assurance: entire sustainability report vs only GHG emissions; and level: limited vs reasonable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical evidence indicates assurance uptake varies (e.g., 40% of Russell 1000 companies obtained some assurance in 2022; only 3% for entire reports; 58% for GHG emissions). Most assurance is limited (92%) with a small portion reasonable (5%). Common assurance standards referenced include ISO 14064-3 (most common), AICPA, AccountAbility's AA1000, IAASB ISAE, and various in-house standards. Service providers vary (accounting firms, boutique consultancies, engineering firms). Registrants should disclose assurance scope, level, standard referenced, and provider to improve investor confidence in accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of material climate-related risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must identify any climate-related risks that have materially impacted or are reasonably likely to have a material impact on the registrant, including on its strategy, results of operations, or financial condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each identified risk, registrants must provide information necessary to understand the nature of the risk and whether it is a physical or transition risk. They must classify whether risks are reasonably likely to manifest in the short-term and in the long-term. For both physical and transition risks, provide detailed information (e.g., particular type of transition risk; geographic location and nature of properties, processes, or operations subject to physical risk). This temporal and categorical classification helps investors assess relevance according to investment horizons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of impacts on strategy, business model, and outlook
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must describe the actual and potential material impacts of any climate-related risks on the registrant's strategy, business model, and outlook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required assessments should, as applicable, address a non-exclusive list of items: business operations; products or services; suppliers, purchasers, or counterparties to material contracts (to the extent known or reasonably available); activities to mitigate or adapt to climate-related risks; and expenditures for research and development. Registrants must also discuss whether and how they consider these impacts as part of strategy, financial planning, and capital allocation. Quantitative and qualitative discussion improves comparability and discourages boilerplate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition plan description and annual updates
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant has adopted a transition plan to manage a material transition risk, it must describe the plan and provide an annual update about any actions taken during the year under the plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual updates must include how expenditures have impacted the registrant's financial condition or results of operations, along with quantitative and qualitative disclosure of material expenditures incurred and material impacts on financial estimates and assumptions as a direct result of the transition plan. The requirement aims to discourage boilerplate, improve comparability over time, and allow investors to analyze impacts across reporting periods. Registrants should explain attribution decisions where linking expenditures to plans is difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenario analysis disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant uses scenario analysis to assess the impact of climate-related risks and, based on results, determines a climate-related risk is reasonably likely to have a material impact, the registrant must describe each such scenario.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions must include a brief description of the parameters, assumptions, and analytical choices used, as well as the expected material impacts on the registrant under each scenario. Because scenario analyses can vary, describing methodology allows investors to assess appropriateness and the registrant's approach to stress-testing across plausible climate and policy futures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal carbon pricing disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If an internal carbon price is material to how a registrant evaluates and manages a material climate-related risk, the registrant must disclose information about the price per metric ton of CO2e in the registrant's reporting currency and the total price, including how the total price is estimated to change over the short-term and long-term, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple internal carbon prices are used, disclose each and explain reasons for using different prices. If the scope of entities/operations for the internal carbon price differs materially from the organizational boundaries used for calculating GHG emissions under Item 1505, describe the difference. These disclosures standardize decision-useful information on how internal pricing affects strategy and financial condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured data, filing treatment, and placement flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules integrate climate-related disclosures into Regulation S-K and S-X frameworks, require structured disclosure (including tagging with XBRL), and treat climate-related disclosures as 'filed' in many cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured data/XBRL tagging enables automated search, retrieval, and comparability across firms and time. Treating disclosures as filed subjects them to potential liability under the Exchange Act and Securities Act, incentivizing accuracy. For disclosures other than financial statement disclosures, registrants retain flexibility to determine appropriate placement within filings, but structured data mitigates concerns about comparability and findability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality qualifiers, phase-in periods, and scaled obligations for smaller registrants
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules include materiality qualifiers (registrants that determine climate risks immaterial have fewer obligations), provide phase-in periods after effective dates, and exempt certain smaller registrants from specific requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EGCs and SRCs receive longer phase-in and are exempt from GHG emissions disclosure requirements. These tailoring measures are intended to reduce compliance burdens for smaller or emerging registrants while preserving investor-relevant disclosures for larger firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits to protect confidential or competitively sensitive information
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules have been narrowed relative to the proposal to avoid requiring disclosure of confidential or competitively sensitive information (for example, elimination of ZIP code-level location disclosures and interim targets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants are given flexibility to describe strategy and exposures in ways that avoid revealing competitively sensitive details while still providing disclosures sufficient for investors to understand exposure to physical risks. This is intended to balance investor benefits with potential competitive harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 3 emissions treatment (not required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope 3 emissions disclosure is no longer required under the final rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal of Scope 3 reduces compliance obligations relative to the proposal. Registrants should note the changed scope when preparing GHG-related disclosures and coordinate with Item 1505 (GHG calculation boundaries) where applicable.
